root_cause: Syntax._get_syntax computed the auto code_width from options.max_width (minus the line-number column) without subtracting horizontal padding. With word_wrap=True the code was wrapped at the full console width, then __rich_console__ wrapped it in Padding, so every wrapped line overflowed by pad_left+pad_right and was cut or re-wrapped (issue #3727 '[BUG] Syntax wrapping doesn't account for padding'). __rich_measure__ already subtracted the padding; the render path did not.
best_solution: In rich/syntax.py Syntax._get_syntax, unpack the padding (`_, right, _, left = Padding.unpack(self.padding)`), subtract left+right from the auto-computed code_width (only when self.code_width is None), and clamp it with max(0, ...). Gold also adds a PaddingProperty descriptor so self.padding is always stored unpacked as a 4-tuple (the issue sets `syntax.padding = (1, 2)` after construction), and changes `if self.padding:` to `if any(self.padding)`. Those two are refactors the hidden test does not need.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that makes the auto code_width equal max_width - numbers_column - pad_left - pad_right when code_width is None, clamped at 0. v7's patch (subtract horizontal padding in both branches, clamp at 0) is such a fix.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_syntax.py::test_padding_plus_wrap: Console(width=24, file=io.StringIO(), legacy_windows=False); Syntax("'Hello, World. This should wrap.'", lexer='python', padding=(0, 3), word_wrap=True); console.print must write exactly "   'Hello, World.       \n   This should wrap.'   \n". The rest of the test patch only adds `-> None` annotations and moves an import. Pre-existing tests test_from_path and test_syntax_guess_lexer are environment-flaky (see our_outcome_summary).
locating_signals: Title 'Syntax padding' names the class (rich/syntax.py Syntax) and the attribute (padding). The linked issue text, which the agent does not see, adds word_wrap and a repro. Grepping `padding` in syntax.py finds __rich_measure__ (subtracts padding) and _get_syntax (does not). The asymmetry between the measure path and the render path is the signal. The gold function is not named.
our_outcome_summary: Kaggle env: all four configs scored FAIL. v4 (163 s, 51 calls) committed only a repo-root test_syntax_padding.py about padding background colour, no source change. v6 (64 s, 24 calls) and v8 (195 s, 39 calls) produced empty patches. v7 (84 s, 20 calls, 1110 chars) made the correct fix in _get_syntax; Kaggle rescore_fair gives resolved=False, exit 1, with no test output captured. Rerun 2026-09-28 on the snapshot with Python 3.12 + Pygments 2.20.0: v7 passes 25/25 in tests/test_syntax.py, base fails only test_padding_plus_wrap. After adding ipython_pygments_lexers==1.1.1 (listed in the Kaggle rescore pip_freeze), test_from_path and test_syntax_guess_lexer flake for gold AND v7 (pygments guess_lexer_for_filename breaks the Python vs IPython tie by set iteration order; gold failed 3 of 8 repeat runs). The v7 FAIL is most likely this flake and the gold oracle PASS was luck. The pod eval3 v7 log shows the same two IPython failures plus 6 Pygments-version render diffs.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only a title like 'X padding' plus an issue link, look for two code paths that compute the same width or size: the measure path and the render path. If one subtracts padding or borders and the other does not, make the render path match, and clamp at 0. Content wrapped inside a Padding or border has to be wrapped to max_width minus the horizontal padding. A bugfix title always needs a source change, so never submit only a new test file or an empty diff. When scoring, rerun any failure several times: tests that depend on plugin discovery or set ordering can flake and make a correct patch look wrong.
